# Signed thin-edge descent and the exact menu-dependent affine moment matrix

The signed rebate mechanism also defeats the n=1,d=4 thin-edge nonnegative-capacity obstruction. This note proves actual descent by a finite body path, and then records the precise affine-moment alternative when several deepest sources are present. The latter keeps the source separator weights dependent on the selected menus.

## 1. A finite-cap envelope lemma

Let K be compact and let F_1(y,t),...,F_m(y,t) be continuous on K times a small parameter interval, differentiable near(y0,0), with

    F_j(y0,0)=Q,
    F_j(y,t)=Q-g_j·(y-y0)+b_j t+o(|y-y0|+|t|).

Assume0 is in the interior of conv{g_j}, and let theta_j>=0, sum theta=1, sum theta_j g_j=0. Suppose y0 is the unique maximizer of min_j F_j(y,0) on K. Then

    max_(y in K) min_j F_j(y,t)
       <=Q+t sum_j theta_j b_j+o(t),  t down to0.     (1)

Proof. The interior convex-hull condition gives c>0 such that max_j g_j·v>=c|v|. Near y0, the minimum is therefore at most Q-(c/2)|y-y0|+C|t|. Uniform convergence and uniqueness force any maximizer y_t to approach y0. Comparing its value with the trial value at y0 then gives |y_t-y0|=O(t). Finally min F_j<=sum theta_j F_j; the linear mark displacement cancels in that average, and the uniform differentiability remainder is o(t). This proves(1). Compactness gives actual maximizers; no unproved differentiability of an optimized mark is used.

## 2. The actual thin-edge body admits a signed rebate

Use the certified small-delta, positive-width body of `candidate e52160c774656005`: central T, identical endpoint D=D_delta, volume v, unique source y0 in T, and the five actual vertex cones. Two high cones J={0,1} capture one endpoint each and have zero outside coarea; the other three cones miss both endpoints. Every actual response menu has positive total high weight theta_J.

A finite balanced menu can be chosen with exactly one cap in each cone. Indeed the continuous response vectors are in R^4, so a balanced law admits a sublaw on at most five vectors; every positive balance must meet all five separated cones. These five vectors span and form a positive circuit. Changing a high cap's base tilt to capture the POSITIVE endpoint and miss the negative one leaves its actual mass and continuous coarea unchanged. The strict saturated choice is available for both high directions. Each low cap can use its strictly missed zero-base-tilt realization. Thus the menu can be chosen so that ALL high caps capture the same endpoint, without disturbing its exact response balance.

Let c be the ordinary centroid of D and use the signed physical field

    Phi(n,z,x)=z h_(D-c)(n).                          (2)

For each normal n it is globally affine in(z,x); its normal dependence is continuous. Its total boundary integral vanishes by reflected-pair cancellation. Every covariance quadratic J_u also vanishes because the paired fibers, centered coordinates, and support factor are identical while the signs are opposite. The central fiber contributes zero. The complete group response is therefore

    integral W Phi dS
       =theta_J integral_(boundary D) h_(D-c)(n)dS
       =theta_J d v>0.                              (3)

The last equality is the ordinary divergence theorem, since h_(D-c)(n)=n·(x-c) at regular boundary points. It includes all facets; no selected-face replacement occurs.

## 3. A valid finite path and actual depth descent

Define endpoint fibers at bases+1 and-1 by

    D_+(t)=c+(1-t)(D-c),
    D_-(t)=c+(1+t)(D-c),

and retain T at base0. Their Minkowski average is exactly D, so their canonical convex hull retains central fiber T. The only sampled bases are-1,0,1 and the extreme fibers remain prescribed. This realizes the inward speeds(2), even if the expanded negative endpoint leaves T individually.

The mixed mass is

    M(t)=|T|+v[(1-t)^d+(1+t)^d],

and the within-fiber covariance numerator is

    |T| Sigma_T+v[(1-t)^(d+2)+(1+t)^(d+2)] Sigma_D.

After division by M(t), the actual pooled covariance remains an even function of t. Hence M'(0)=0 and every covariance-width derivative is zero.

Freeze the five selected actual cap normals and let F_j(y,t) be their actual masses through a candidate point y in T. Their strict outside margins persist near(y0,0). A high cap captures exactly the shrinking endpoint and has derivative -dv; a low cap captures no endpoint and has derivative zero. Their own T integrals change only through the mark and the covariance width; the latter has derivative zero. Thus

    F_j(y,t)=Q-S_j u_j·(y-y0)-dv 1_(j in J)t
                       +o(|y-y0|+t).

The five response vectors S_j u_j positively span R^4. The frozen caps have unique common deepest mark y0: every nonzero displacement raises at least one threshold, causing strict own cap loss and no outside increase. Applying(1) gives

    max_(y in T) min_j F_j(y,t)
       <=Q-dv theta_J t+o(t).                        (4)

The actual depth is bounded above by this frozen-menu envelope. The two exposed endpoints remain far below Q for small t, because their entire volumes tend to v<Q. Consequently the actual global normalized depth satisfies

    beta(C_t)<=beta(C_0)-[dv theta_J/M(0)]t+o(t).

This is strict actual descent. It neither assumes a differentiable source trajectory nor discards the covariance term. The thin-edge nonnegative-capacity obstruction is therefore also nonstationary for the signed cone.

## 4. The exact finite affine-moment alternative for several sources

Now work in the general attained pure-width interface with actual deepest sources i=1,...,k and common normalized depth beta. Fix a complete choice of active balanced response menus nu_i, with weights theta_ij, sum_j theta_ij=1 and sum_j theta_ij S_ij u_ij=0. Normalize Gamma(u_ij)=1.

Choose finitely many REALIZABLE affine physical fields F_1,...,F_m such that their entire linear span is admissible. In particular both signs of every span element are allowed. This hypothesis avoids treating arbitrary independent normal motions as automatically realizable.

For each field F_l define the actual linear response quantities

    D_l=integral F_l dS,
    J_ij,l=integral [u_ij·(X-g_z)]^2 F_l dS,
    B_ij,l=integral Psi(q_ij)F_l dS.

The complete affine response row of source i is the vector r_i in R^m with components

    r_i,l = sum_j theta_ij
              [B_ij,l+A_ij(D_l-J_ij,l)/(2M)]-beta D_l. (5)

This is the exact covariance formula from `candidate 6e754f2bf13bdbd1`. The width moments A_ij, own source response and normalization are all retained.

There is an affine field in this span that strictly improves EVERY source group if and only if

    0 not in conv{r_1,...,r_k}.                       (6)

Indeed a coefficient vector b produces improvement b·r_i at source i. If zero lies outside the compact finite convex hull, strict separation gives b·r_i>0 for every i. Conversely, any convex weights lambda with sum_i lambda_i r_i=0 exclude simultaneous strict positivity. This proves both directions of(6).

Thus at an actual body minimum, for this FIXED complete menu choice there must exist

    lambda_i>=0, sum_i lambda_i=1,
    sum_i lambda_i r_i=0.                            (7)

For one source, (7) forces its complete affine response row to vanish. The two signed constructions above exhibit a favorable menu for which it does not vanish and therefore produce descent.

## 5. Menu choice is retained; no universal lambda is asserted

Let R_i be the set of response rows(5) obtainable from balanced actual menus at source i. Under the standard compact active-cap representatives and positive-coarea bounds, this is a compact convex set: the menu constraints are closed linear constraints on probability measures, and(5) is a continuous linear image.

The affine necessary condition at a body minimum is

    for EVERY choice r_i in R_i,
    there EXISTS lambda(r_1,...,r_k) satisfying(7).   (8)

Equivalently, for every coefficient vector b there is at least one source i such that

    sup_(r in R_i) b·r <=0.                          (9)

To check equivalence, failure of(9) supplies a positive response choice independently at every source and hence violates(8) by separation. Conversely, if one menu selection has zero outside its row convex hull, its separating b has strictly positive support value at every source, violating(9).

This is a useful exact matrix formulation of the multi-source obstruction. It does NOT permit a source separator lambda chosen once for every menu choice. Even the scalar row sets R_1=[1,2] and R_2={-1} satisfy(8), while their cancelling lambda varies with r_1. Any proposed sourcewise bound on lambda must be proved for a favorable actual joint menu, with the complete response(5), rather than imported from a fixed nonnegative-field capacity.

# Signed thin-edge descent and the exact menu-dependent affine moment matrix

**Menu-dependent affine response separation**

Work in the attained pure outward-smoothed model of the source and fix a complete finite list of source menus. Choose finitely many realizable affine physical fields whose entire linear span is admissible in both signs. For each menu, form its row of normalized first responses, using the source's boundary, covariance, and total-mass terms. There is a single signed affine direction making every menu response strictly negative exactly when zero is outside the convex hull of these rows. Consequently an actual local minimum forces zero into that convex hull for each such complete menu choice. The resulting nonnegative balancing coefficients may depend on the menu choice.

Scope limits: An exact finite-dimensional alternative with menu-dependent quantifiers, not a new arithmetic or Gamma-capacity inequality.
